description: Workshop benchmark for the three WHO guideline documents already indexed by this repository. Questions are educational and never patient-specific.

cases.query: At acute health care facility level, what does WHO recommend about workload, staffing and bed occupancy, and why does this matter for infection prevention and control?
cases.ground_truth: WHO treats workload, staffing and bed occupancy as a core IPC component. Staffing should be appropriate for patient workload, and bed occupancy should not exceed the facility's standard capacity, with one patient per bed and adequate spacing. These organizational conditions affect the risk of health care-associated infection and the ability to apply IPC practices reliably.

required_answer_parts.description: identify workload, staffing and bed occupancy as a facility-level IPC core component
explain that staffing should match patient workload
state the bed-capacity, one-patient-per-bed or spacing recommendation
connect these conditions to IPC or health care-associated infection risk

expected_evidence_groups.name: WHO IPC core-components guideline
any_of: Guidelines on core components of infection prevention and control programmes at the national and acute health care facility level

cases.query: According to the WHO guideline for adults, at what confirmed blood pressure should pharmacological treatment usually start, and what treatment target is recommended for people without comorbidities?
cases.ground_truth: WHO recommends starting pharmacological antihypertensive treatment for people with a confirmed diagnosis of hypertension at a systolic blood pressure of at least 140 mmHg or a diastolic blood pressure of at least 90 mmHg. For people with hypertension and no comorbidities, the recommended treatment target is below 140/90 mmHg.

required_answer_parts.description: make clear that the treatment threshold applies to a confirmed diagnosis
state the 140 mmHg systolic or 90 mmHg diastolic initiation threshold
state the below 140/90 mmHg target for people without comorbidities

expected_evidence_groups.name: WHO hypertension guideline
any_of: Guideline for the pharmacological treatment of hypertension in adults

cases.query: According to WHO HEARTS-D, which blood tests can be used to diagnose type 2 diabetes, and why should an abnormal result in a person without symptoms be confirmed?
cases.ground_truth: WHO HEARTS-D describes diagnosis using plasma glucose testing, including fasting plasma glucose, a two-hour oral glucose tolerance test, or random plasma glucose when classic symptoms are present, and it also describes HbA1c where appropriate. In a person without symptoms, an abnormal result should be repeated or confirmed on another day to reduce the risk of a false diagnosis.

required_answer_parts.description: name fasting, two-hour oral glucose tolerance or symptom-linked random plasma glucose testing
mention HbA1c as a diagnostic option where appropriate
explain that an asymptomatic abnormal result should be repeated or confirmed

expected_evidence_groups.name: WHO HEARTS-D guideline
any_of: HEARTS D: Diagnosis and management of type 2 diabetes
